encounters.cc: Irregular menstrual cycles and worsening acne with new onset hirsutism

lines: Irregular menstrual cycles and worsening acne with new onset hirsutism
She has had infrequent periods since menarche at age 12 and now menstruates every 2 to 3 months.
Over the past year, she has also noticed dark, coarse hairs growing on her chin and lower abdomen, which she finds embarrassing.
She denies galactorrhea, headaches, vision problems, or recent weight loss.
She is not currently sexually active and is not interested in becoming pregnant.
Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable.
- Maternal aunt with polycystic ovary syndrome
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks per month).
She has moderate inflammatory acne along her jawline and terminal hair on the upper lip and below the umbilicus.
A urine pregnancy test is negative. Laboratory testing shows normal TSH and prolactin.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows bilateral ovarian enlargement with numerous small follicles located peripherally.
The clinician suspects an underlying endocrine abnormality

encounters.cc: Irregular menstrual cycles and concerns regarding sexual health

lines: Irregular menstrual cycles and concerns regarding sexual health
27-year-old female with PCOS, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and obesity returns for follow-up three months after her initial visit with ongoing irregular menstrual cycles and sexual health concerns.
She reports that for the past two years, her periods have occurred every 35 to 60 days and are often unpredictable.
She also notes worsening acne since her late teens and sometimes notices coarse hairs growing on her chin and lower abdomen.
She has been sexually active with her boyfriend of two years and is not using contraception, but has not become pregnant.
Her medical history is otherwise unremarkable.
She does not take any medications or supplements.
- Maternal aunt with polycystic ovary syndrome
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks per month).
On examination, her BMI is 27 kg/m². Her blood pressure is normal.
She has moderate acne on her cheeks and jawline, and there is visible terminal hair on her chin and linea alba.
A serum pregnancy test is negative.
A pelvic ultrasound reveals a normal-sized uterus with slightly enlarged ovaries containing multiple small peripheral follicles.
She is scheduled to follow up in several weeks to discuss fertility and menstrual regulation options.

encounters.cc: Inability to conceive after one year of unprotected intercourse

lines: Inability to conceive after one year of unprotected intercourse
The patient returns with known polycystic ovary syndrome following prior endocrinology care.
Her partner, a 30-year-old male, has a normal semen analysis.
She inquires about the impact of caffeine on her fertility.
- Maternal aunt with polycystic ovary syndrome
The patient reports drinking 2 cups of coffee daily.
Vital signs are within normal limits
The physician recalls a recent study that evaluated the association between caffeine intake and fecundability, measured by the odds ratio (OR).
The study reported an OR of 0.8 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.7 to 0.9 for the association between caffeine intake and fecundability.

encounters.cc: Severe headaches and transient episodes of vision loss

lines: Severe headaches and transient episodes of vision loss

This 30-year-old female with polycystic ovary syndrome, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and obesity, previously evaluated for infertility, presents with a two-week history of headaches and transient episodes of vision loss lasting a few seconds, especially when she stands up quickly or changes her head position.
Her medical history is significant for obesity and a recent diagnosis of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
- Maternal aunt with polycystic ovary syndrome
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks per month).
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm, and BMI is 32 kg/m^2
Fundoscopic examination reveals bilateral optic disc swelling with blurred margins.
Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, and there is no relative afferent pupillary defect.
The remainder of the neurological examination is unremarkable.
No neck stiffness or photophobia is noted.
